newsitem.title: UK: UK okays Centrica, NGC deal on Accor.
newsitem.headline: UK okays Centrica, NGC deal on Accor.

text.p: The British Office of Fair Trading (OFT) has given the go ahead to Centrica plc taking a controlling interest in gas trader and shipper Accord Energy Ltd, a joint venture with NGC Corporation of the United States, Centrica said in a statement on Tuesday.

Accord, which principally trades in short-term gas in the wholesale market, will continue operations as before under managing director Jake Ulrich and will be based at Centrica's corporate offices in Slough, England.

Accord was set up in 1994 with the share capital divided into 51 percent for British Gas and 49 percent for NGC UK Ltd. The shares carried equal voting rights and NGC UK Limited and British Gas plc each undertook not to compete with Accord for the duration of the joint venture.

As British Gas prepared for demerger into Centrica plc and BG plc, its shareholding in Accord was transferred to GB Gas Holdings Limited, now wholly owned by Centrica. British Gas plc also held shares in NGC Corporation, which are now held by BG plc.
NGC Corporation will now be allowed to compete with Accord with immediate effect.
